pride_data.title: A hierarchical assembly pathway directs the unique subunit arrangement of TRiC/CCT
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study assembly intermediates of the chaperonin TRiC/CCT. Complex were cross-linked with the homobifunctional, noncleavable reagent, disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS).
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking using DSS (d0/d12, Creative Molecules) was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin. Digests were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography and SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Elite system. Duplicate injections of three SEC fractions were performed. Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of target proteins and identified contaminants. Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for common ions, 0.3 Da for fragment containing the cross-link. Only lysine residues were considered as possible cross-linking sites. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used. False discovery rates (FDRs) were controlled by searches against shuffled sequences of all reversed database entries. The FDR was set to <5% at the non-redundant peptide-pair level. Cross-linking identifications are compiled in spreadsheets in Microsoft Excel format that are included with the submission.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; protein folding; chaperonin; tric/cct
